did_you_know.text: Did you know? The Israelites swore at Mizpah that they would not give their daughters in marriage to the men of Benjamin—a vow that later became a serious problem when the tribe of Benjamin was nearly wiped out.

Did you know? The Israelites went to Bethel and sat there before God. They raised their voices and wept bitterly. The next day, they built an altar there and offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings.

Did you know? The Israelites had decreed that anyone who failed to come before the assembly at Mizpah would be put to death. When they checked who was absent from the gathering, they discovered that the people of Jabesh-gilead had not come.

Did you know? The assembly sent twelve thousand fighting men to Jabesh-gilead and ordered them to kill its inhabitants and destroy the women and children, in keeping with its decision against those who had not taken part in the gathering.
Did you know? Among the people of Jabesh-gilead, the Israelites found four hundred young women who were virgins and had never slept with a man, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh.

Did you know? The Benjaminites came out from the rock of Rimmon and received the four hundred women rescued from Jabesh-gilead, but there were still not enough women for all the remaining men of the tribe.
Did you know? The elders proposed a solution involving a festival held at Shiloh, which was described as a place south of the road that goes up from Bethel to Shechem and north of Lebonah.
Did you know? According to the plan, the Benjaminites were to hide in the vineyards and seize wives for themselves from among the women of Shiloh when they came out to dance during the festival.
Did you know? The Benjaminites followed the plan, taking women from among the dancers and returning to their inheritance. They then rebuilt the cities and settled in them.
Did you know? The final verse of Judges repeats the central idea of the period described in the book: there was no king in Israel, and everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
